page.title: Listen: killer whales and their neighbours on the MARS hydrophone
page.subtitle: MBARI MARS cabled hydrophone, 891 m depth, Monterey Canyon · from perch-hoplite-orcas-MBNMS
page.lead: A few confirmed examples of each class, to give an ear for what the labels contain. Each is shown twice: the 5-second window the classifier scores, and 30 seconds of surrounding context with that window marked. Listen to both. The context answers questions the window cannot — whether a call is part of one animal's bout, whether it differs from what surrounds it, whether it stands alone, and whether ship noise is masking it. Audio is peak-normalized for playback; the raw recordings are far too quiet to hear.
page.footer: These are a handful of examples, not the dataset. All 1,351 confirmed windows are listed with their recording and offset in the repository's labels/ directory, and any of them can be regenerated from the public raw audio. Confirmed by ear by D. Edgington; humpback labels verified by J. P. Ryan. Raw recordings are free and public via the AWS Open Data registry (Pacific Ocean Sound). Spectrograms use the same code and settings as the project's annotation interface — mel, viridis, 80 dB range. See the repository and DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22574816.

cards.title: Killer whale — 12 May 2018, the densest day in the archive
cards.note: 181 confirmed calls on this day alone. Bigg's killer whale calls arrive as brief discrete bursts rather than continuous song, which is why the context here sounds punctuated rather than sustained.

cards.title: Killer whale — 13 April 2018, morning hunting event
cards.note: The first orca activity this project identified, and the event that started the work.

cards.title: Humpback whale — 28 October 2020
cards.note: Peak humpback season, and the busiest humpback day in the labeled set. Note how much the context adds: humpback vocalization is often continuous where orca is not.

cards.title: Dolphin — 13 April 2018
cards.note: Recorded the same morning as the confirmed killer whale event above, which makes the comparison a useful one.

cards.title: Ship noise — 4 April 2018
cards.note: Broadband and mechanical. Worth hearing because it is what masks biological calls — one of the questions the context panel is there to answer.

cards.title: Other — 13 April 2018
cards.note: A real sound that fits no named class. Not silence: quiet background is a separate label that never appears as a detection.
